identity.title: Deep Herschel observations of the 2 Jy sample: assessing the non-thermal and AGN contributions to the far-IR continuum
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present the results of *Herschel* PACS and SPIRE observations of a complete sample of 46 powerful 2Jy radio AGN at intermediate redshifts ($0.05 < z < 0.7$), which represent the deepest pointed observations of a major sample of radio AGN undertaken by *Herschel*.
In order to assess the importance of non-thermal synchrotron emission at far-IR wavelengths, we also present new *APEX* sub-mm and *ALMA* mm data.
Here we concentrate on the continuum observations that were taken as a by-product of the molecular line observations.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure Herschel PACS and SPIRE far-IR photometry and deblend confused sources

method.value: Processed PACS images in HIPE 14.2 with ScanmapPhotProject using aperture photometry (10 or 5 arcsec radius); extracted SPIRE fluxes from level 2 archive products with sourceExtractorSussextractor PRF fitting; deblended confused sources using GetSources.

key_parameters.value: PACS apertures: 10 arcsec radius (or 5 arcsec for faint <20 mJy / confused sources); 48 blank sky apertures for uncertainty

findings_qualitative.value: Non-thermal synchrotron contamination in the far-IR is strongest in CSS/GPS sources (from lobes/hotspots), WLRG/FRI sources (from cores), and BLRG/Q sources (from beamed cores).

evidence.quote: Non-thermal contamination is strongest in objects with compact CSS/GPS or extended FRI radio morphologies, and in those with type 1 optical spectra.

findings_qualitative.value: Selecting radio AGN on the basis of a steep low-frequency radio spectral index does not prevent significant non-thermal core or lobe contamination at far-IR wavelengths.

evidence.quote: This emphasises that selection on the basis of a steep radio spectral index is not by itself sufficient to avoid non-thermal contamination in the far-IR.

findings_qualitative.value: Strong correlations between 100 and 160 um luminosities and AGN bolometric power indicators (L_[OIII] and L_24) persist after removing non-thermally contaminated and strongly star-forming galaxies, supporting AGN radiative heating of cool dust.

evidence.quote: Finally, concentrating on the subset of objects that lack independent evidence for strong star formation activity, and for which the non-thermal contamination in the PACS bands is negligible or can be corrected, we find highly significant correlations between the 100 and 160$\mu$m monochromatic continuum luminosities ($L_{100}$ and $L_{160}$) and AGN bolometric power indicators ($L_{[OIII]}$ and $L_{24}$).

claims.hypothesis: Steep radio spectrum selection (alpha > 0.5 between 2.7 and 4.8 GHz) avoids non-thermal synchrotron contamination of the far-IR continuum in powerful radio AGN.
claims.experiment: Constructed radio-to-IR SEDs for the complete 46-object southern 2Jy sample using new Herschel PACS/SPIRE, APEX LABOCA 870 um, and ALMA ~100 GHz continuum data, and evaluated core and lobe/hotspot extrapolation into the far-IR.
claims.result: 28-43% of the sample in PACS bands (<200 um) and 30-72% in SPIRE bands (>200 um) suffer significant or potential non-thermal contamination from cores or compact lobes.
claims.finding: Steep radio spectrum selection is not sufficient by itself to avoid non-thermal synchrotron contamination at far-IR wavelengths.

evidence.quote: Therefore, it is clear that selection on the basis of a steep radio spectrum does not entirely avoid the inclusion in radio AGN samples of some objects that are dominated by non-thermal emission at far-IR wavelengths.

Despite the fact that all the objects in our sample were selected to have SEDs that are steeply declining with frequency at radio wavelengths, a significant fraction show evidence for non-thermal contamination in the far-IR, with the incidence of contamination higher in the longer-wavelength SPIRE bands (30 – 72%) than in the shorter wavelength PACS bands (28 – 43%).

claims.hypothesis: The incidence and origin of non-thermal far-IR contamination depend on the radio morphology and optical spectroscopic classification of the AGN.
claims.experiment: Classified non-thermal lobe/hotspot and core contamination across CSS/GPS, FRII, FRI, BLRG/Q, NLRG, and WLRG sub-classes in Table 2.
claims.result: 5/7 CSS/GPS sources have strong lobe/hotspot contamination; 6/6 WLRG/FRI sources have core contamination (4/6 dominated); 8/13 (61%) BLRG/Q/FRII show core contamination compared to 6/15 (40%) NLRG/FRII.
claims.finding: Non-thermal contamination is strongly linked to radio/optical class, consistent with young compact lobes in CSS/GPS, beamed inner jets in BLRG/Q, and non-thermal core dominance with weak/absent tori in WLRG/FRI.

evidence.loc: Dependence of non-thermal contamination on radio/optical class
evidence.quote: Indeed, 5/7 of the CSS/GPS sources in our sample have substantial non-thermal lobe/hotspot emission at far-IR wavelengths

evidence.loc: Dependence of non-thermal contamination on radio/optical class
evidence.quote: Therefore, 8 out of 13 (61%) of BLRG/FRII in the 2Jy sample are identified with clear or potential non-thermal core contamination to some part of their far-IR SED.

evidence.loc: Dependence of non-thermal contamination on radio/optical class
evidence.quote: Looking at the WLRG/FRI objects in Table [\[tab:NTcontam\]](#tab:NTcontam), it is notable that all 6 such objects have contamination from non-thermal core emission in their infrared SED.

claims.hypothesis: Radiation from the AGN is an important heating source for the cool, far-IR (100 and 160 um) emitting dust in powerful radio AGN.
claims.experiment: Calculated Spearman rank and partial rank correlations (controlling for redshift) between rest-frame L_100, L_160 and AGN power indicators L_[OIII], L_24 after excluding non-thermally contaminated and strongly star-forming (RSF) sources (N=26).
claims.result: Highly significant partial rank correlations (p < 0.5%) are found for L_[OIII] vs L_100 (rho = 0.764), L_[OIII] vs L_160 (rho = 0.478), L_24 vs L_100 (rho = 0.823), and L_24 vs L_160 (rho = 0.672).
claims.finding: Far-IR continuum luminosities correlate strongly with intrinsic AGN power, providing evidence for AGN radiative heating of cool dust, though an indirect correlation between low-level star formation and AGN accretion cannot be completely ruled out.

evidence.loc: Correlations between far-IR luminosities and AGN power indicators
evidence.quote: The results are presented in the bottom part of Table [1](#tab:correlations), and show that all the correlation statistics, including the partial rank correlation statistics, suggest highly significant correlations between the 100 and 160$\mu$m luminosities and intrinsic AGN power.

This provides further evidence that radiation from the AGN is an important heating source for the cool, far-IR emitting dust in many radio AGN, although we cannot entirely rule out the idea that the correlations arise through a strong relationship between star formation activity and AGN power.

evidence.quote: This has led to a data set that is not uniform across the sample in its completeness and depth

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot completely rule out that far-IR vs AGN power correlations arise indirectly from a mutual correlation between undetected moderate star formation and AGN accretion.

evidence.loc: Correlations between far-IR luminosities and AGN power indicators
evidence.quote: On the other hand, our observations do not entirely rule out some level of heating of the cool dust by regions of star formation, even in cases that currently lack strong independent evidence for recent star formation activity.

referee_caveats_inferred: Multi-epoch variability across a 15-year baseline (Spitzer 2004-2007, VLA/ATCA 2006, Herschel/LABOCA 2011-2013, ALMA 2016/2019) introduces unquantified systematic uncertainty into SED extrapolations of flat-spectrum radio cores.
ALMA compact configuration resolution (1.4-3.7 arcsec) could include inner kpc-scale jet/lobe emission in addition to the nuclear core (explicitly noted for PKS 2314+03).

data_public_as_stated.value: Herschel and ALMA data are public in their respective archives; APEX LABOCA data available on reasonable request to the authors.

evidence.quote: The Herschel data underlying this article are available in the ESA Herschel Science Archive, at http://archives.esac.esa.int/hsa/whsa/. The ALMA data from this article are available in the ALMA Archive, at https://almascience.nrao.edu/alma-data. The APEX LABOCA data presented in this article can be shared on reasonable request to the authors.

products_in_archive.value: Standard pipeline-processed average continuum images in the ALMA archive and level 2 SPIRE maps in the Herschel archive were used directly.

evidence.quote: Non-thermal core continuum fluxes for the observed 2Jy sources were measured from the standard pipeline-processed average continuum images available from the *ALMA* archive.
however with HIPE14 and the updated calibration we choose to use the default pipeline processed point source and extended maps from the *Herschel* archive for the analysis

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB (standard ALMA archive continuum images for 29 targets and Herschel PACS/SPIRE maps for 46 targets; raw ALMA CO(1-0) visibilities not needed)
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA core fluxes are measured directly as peak mJy/beam from public pipeline-processed archive continuum images, and all photometric fluxes are tabulated in Table 1, though APEX LABOCA data are only available on request and some per-object fitting/aperture choices are not fully specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA part is trivial to reproduce from public archival pipeline continuum images (peak flux measurement of 29 targets), and the main photometric and correlation tables provide clear numeric benchmarks.
